2607.28466.title: A report-grounded vision-language foundation model for colonoscopy from 280000 routine reports
2607.28466.paper_summary: Vision-language models remain underused in colonoscopy despite the rich expert descriptions recorded in routine reports. These reports document lesion appearance, size and location but summarise entire procedures rather than caption individual frames, leaving clinical findings only weakly linked to the corresponding images. Here we develop EndoCLIP, a colonoscopy vision-language foundation model trained on 125,756 lesion-level image-text pairs progressively recovered from 280,476 routine colonoscopy records. Across lesion-level image-text retrieval, structured report generation and six multi-centre clinical classification tasks, EndoCLIP outperforms general-purpose and biomedical vision-language encoders in both zero-shot and linear-probe settings. On benign-versus-malignant classification, its linear probe approaches the performance of expert readers in a blinded study involving 12 endoscopists. These results suggest that recovering finding-to-frame correspondence can transform routine documentation into scalable supervision, enabling clinical targets to be specified in language rather than separately annotated for each task.
2607.28466.paper_summary_zh: 視覺-語言模型在結腸鏡檢查中仍然未被充分利用，儘管在常規報告中記錄了豐富的專家描述。這些報告記錄病變的外觀、大小和位置，但總結整個程序，而不是對單個幀進行標註，導致臨床發現與相應圖像之間的聯繫僅僅是微弱的。在這裡，我們開發了 EndoCLIP，一個結腸鏡檢查視覺-語言基礎模型，該模型在 125,756 個病變級別的圖像-文本對上進行訓練，這些對逐步從 280,476 份常規結腸鏡檢查記錄中恢復而來。在病變級別的圖像-文本檢索、結構化報告生成和六個多中心臨床分類任務中，EndoCLIP 在零-shot 和線性探測設置下均超越了通用和生物醫學視覺-語言編碼器。在良性與惡性分類中，其線性探測接近於在涉及 12 名內鏡醫生的盲測研究中專家讀者的表現。這些結果表明，恢復發現與幀之間的對應關係可以將常規文檔轉變為可擴展的監督，從而使臨床目標能夠用語言指定，而不是為每個任務單獨註釋。
